verdict.rationale: Apple's first-party docs specify external connectivity: Thunderbolt 5 at up to 120Gb/s, external display limits over Thunderbolt and HDMI, and RDMA over Thunderbolt for multi-Mac setups. That is enough to plan a dock around, but the evidence never covers PCIe generation or lanes, or internal storage speed. missing for 10: PCIe generation/lane counts, fast storage specs (SSD throughput/capacity), port count/layout details, independent hands-on corroboration of I/O throughput.

support.subject: As a developer, the platform has documented I/O headroom — PCIe generation and lanes, fast storage, and external connectivity specs I can plan a build or dock setup around

citations.quote: M4 Pro also supports Thunderbolt 5 on Mac, delivering up to 120Gb/s data transfer speeds, which more than doubles the throughput of Thunderbolt 4.

Up to two external displays with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt, or one external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt and one external display with up to 4K resolution at 144Hz over HDMI
the 14- and 16-inch models with M4 Pro and M4 Max offer Thunderbolt 5 for faster transfer speeds and advanced connectivity
can scale training across multiple Macs with RDMA over Thunderbolt
